styles.label: Springs
styles.blurb: Baotu Spring, Daming Lake and the city's famous waters.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Shandong Museum, old streets and the thousand-year springs.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Lu cuisine, street snacks and spring-side teahouses.

stays.why: Walk to Daming Lake, Baotu Spring and the old streets; best base for first-timers.
Cheapest and easiest for early trains; a short taxi or bus to the lake sights.
Newer hotels near the stadium and east-side sights; good metro line 3 access.
Quiet business hotels in the east; only worth it if you have work there.

food: Try Lu cuisine (Shandong food): braised dishes, sweet-and-sour carp and spring-onion pancakes. Portions are big; share.
Street snacks: jianbing (savoury crepe), grilled skewers and baozi. A snack meal is often ¥10–30.
Look for spring-water teahouses near Baotu Spring; tea is usually ¥30–80 per pot.
Night markets and food streets around the old city and university areas are busiest after 6pm.
Mid-range restaurant meals run about ¥50–120 per person; check prices on the menu before ordering.
more_time: Add a day trip to Mount Tai (Taishan) in Tai'an: about 30–60 minutes by high-speed train; check times on the day.
History fans can swap a city afternoon for the Shandong Museum; entry is usually free but check opening days.
Slow down at Daming Lake: a boat ride and a walk along the old streets can fill a relaxed half day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the springs, the lake and the old streets at an easy pace; add a night for a Mount Tai day trip.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 5°C and lows around -4°C. Pack a warm coat; few rainy days.
February: still cold, highs around 9°C. Short days; indoor sights are a good bet.
March: warming to about 16°C. Good for walking the lake and springs; a few wet days.
April: pleasant, highs near 22°C. One of the best months for outdoor sightseeing.
May: warm at about 27°C. Comfortable mornings; carry water and sun protection.
June: hot, highs near 32°C. Sightsee early and rest in the afternoon.
July: hottest and wettest, highs around 32°C with about 14 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
August: hot and rainy, similar to July. Plan indoor backups.
September: cools to about 27°C. A strong month for the springs and lake.
October: mild at about 20°C. Arguably the best month; clear and comfortable.
November: cooler, highs near 13°C. Fewer crowds; bring a jacket.
December: cold again, highs around 6°C. Quiet season; wrap up warm.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold dry winters, hot humid summers with the most rain, and pleasant spring and autumn.

items.title: Best time: April to May and September to October
items.text: Mild highs of about 20–27°C. Ideal for the springs, Daming Lake and walking the old streets.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (June to August)
items.text: Highs near 32°C with lows around 22–24°C. Go out early or after sunset.

items.title: Rain peaks in July and August
items.text: About 13–14 rain days each month. Pack a light umbrella and a waterproof layer.

items.title: Cold, dry winter (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 5–9°C and lows down to -4°C. Very few rainy days; wear a warm coat.

items.title: Spring can be breezy and dry
items.text: March to May warms quickly with only a few wet days. A light jacket helps on windy days.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for spring and autumn, a warm coat for winter, and light breathable clothes plus an umbrella for summer.

transit.best: Metro and buses for cheap trips; taxis or Didi when you don't speak Chinese.

modes.text: Three lines (1, 2, 3) cover west, east and north. No line through the city centre yet, so you may still need a bus or taxi.
¥1 or ¥2 for air-conditioned buses. Use a transit card or Apple Pay for a discount.
Taxis flag at ¥7.50. Drivers rarely speak English, so have your destination in Chinese. Didi works well.
Not recommended for visitors: traffic and parking are difficult.
The city centre around Daming Lake is walkable. Shared bikes are available but need an app.
